params.body:
## Why

A business rule is a claim. Until today the `Stand` column (klant, code, betwist) was typed by hand next to a free-text `Code` column, and R S3-3.2 ("Car-Pass allows one registration per day") stood as `betwist` for six days with "externe regel" as its only source, while the Car-Pass Inflow Specification, public and one fetch away, says exactly what it means. This applies the same three laws `Report\Gate` applies to a sentence of Elixir to a sentence about the platform: a claim carries its facts, a number in a sentence must be a fact, and a verifier refuses otherwise.

## What changes

- **One column `Bron`** (was `Code`) on every rule row, holding typed references: `wet:<id>#<anchor>` (a quoted passage in `docs/bedrijfsregels/bronnen/<id>.md`), `klant:V-4` (an answered acceptance-test question), `klant:beslissingen#v-4` (a dated decision), `klant:werksessie-2026-09-11` (the session the first version came from), `code:Class::member` / path, and `~type:ref` for a source that contradicts the rule. Loose notes ("te zoeken") stay visible but are not sources. The table keeps five cells, so `bin/rules-coverage`, `bin/rules-page` and the existing tests keep parsing.
- **The stand is derived, never typed**: a contradicting source makes `betwist`; else a resolving `wet:` makes `wet`; else `klant:`; else `code:`; no resolving source is `betwist` (nobody stands for it). `vervallen` and `wens` stay by hand. `bin/rules-sources --write` rewrites the column; the old `extern`, `test`, `Shane` and `open` stands are gone.
- **Numbers are facts**: every number in a rule (digits or a Dutch number word; not rule/finding/question codes or dates) must appear in a cited source: the quoted passage for `wet:`/`klant:`, the file for `code:`. Strict in the sourced chapters (S3) and for every rule that cites a quoted passage; elsewhere a warning listed by `bin/rules-sources --numbers` (60 rules), because 700 rules predate the check and a code file is a weak witness for a number.
- **`bin/rules-sources.php`** (shared library) and **`bin/rules-sources`** (CLI: check, `--write`, `--list`, `--numbers`). **`tests/Feature/RulesSourcesTest.php`** fails with the rule code and the missing piece: a passage anchor that does not exist, a class without that member, a V-number not in the acceptance test, a stand that does not follow, an uncovered number.
- **`bin/rules-coverage`** gains "Met bron" and "Wet" columns; **`bin/rules-page`** renders the sources as footnotes under each rule, the quoted passage unfolding inline with a link to the source.
- **Mechanical migration of the old `Code` column** in every chapter to `code:` entries (backtick typos, line numbers and parenthetical notes normalised). The resolver caught 41 references to code that had moved or vanished (facade vs model name clashes, `PublicVehicleApi` that is a test class, `VehicleObserver::triggerWebhook` now in `VehiclePublisher`, ...); those are repointed. Existing `klant` rows cite the session; existing `betwist` rows keep their stand through `~code:` markers. No `wet:`/`klant:` sources were invented outside S3.

## Pilot: S3 Car-Pass

- `bronnen/car-pass-inflow.md`: the Car-Pass Inflow Specification (page version 153 of 2026-09-15, read 2026-09-17), quoted verbatim under 26 anchors: scope up to 3,5 t, exact odometer, duplicate readings, security, environments, statuses, REVIEWING and issue 129, WAITING_FOR_DIV, polling (1 per 10 s, 90 s), confirmation a day late, manual correction, the deprecated `status/vhr`, issue 131 and the 2026 unknown-vehicle flow, the issue table (001, 123, 124, 128, 129, 130, 131, 207, 208, 209), the VHR obligations, 6-month validity, the paid Car-Pass document (11,10 EUR).
- `bronnen/beslissingen.md`: V-4 (Shane, 2026-09-17: count ourselves, grey the button, show every refusal) and V-5 (Ilse, 2026-09-17, optie A: renewal stays automatic with the sheet mileage; the vehicle re-enters the work list at every expiry).
- Stand changes in S3 (13 of 74 rules): R S3-2.4 betwist -> wet (rewritten to the spec: VIN + odometer of the day, `firstUseDate` optional, X-48); R S3-3.1 betwist -> wet (rewritten to the issue table and the manual-correction rule); R S3-3.2 betwist -> wet (the exact Car-Pass wording: same user, same vehicle, same `odometerReadingDate`, issue 123); R S3-3.7 code -> klant (V-4); R S3-5.1 betwist -> klant (V-5); R S3-8.1 to S3-8.8 extern -> wet, each on its passage; new R S3-8.9 (6-month validity) as the wet source behind the work list.
- Still `betwist` in S3, honestly: R S3-2.8 (X-23, unreachable AUTHENTICATION_ERROR branch), R S3-2.10 (X-50, there is no lock any more; no source), R S3-4.4 (X-49, no Hexon export; the URL goes to Modix).
- Findings: X-04 (one registration per day) resolved as documentation, the UI change is a separate PR; X-03 (correction only via the portal) resolved, the Livewire list has the correction/confirm dialog; X-05 (seven days) now `beslist: Ilse`, open for the code part only (re-entry at every expiry).

## Not in this PR

The UI change that counts registrations and greys the button (R S3-3.7), the work-list re-entry at every expiry (R S3-5.1), sourcing the other chapters, and `klant:V-n` for the other answered questions. `docs/acceptatietest.md` is read directly for V-numbers instead of a generated copy in `bronnen/`, so there is one truth for a question.

## Tests

`RulesSourcesTest`, `RulesIdentityTest`, `RulesCoverageTest`, `RulesDocsBuildTest`: 14 tests, 48 assertions, green. `bin/rules-coverage`, `bin/rules-page` and `bin/rules-sources` run clean.
params.title: Business rules carry their sources; the status is derived, S3 Car-Pass as the pilot
